content.text: Our shop keeps carts in a 4 KB session cookie and long carts get cut short. Compare keeping carts in Redis or in Postgres in a short paragraph, recommend one, and leave the choice to me. Do not read or write any files.

Moving carts out of the cookie and into a server-side store fixes the 4 KB limit either way. The cookie then holds only a cart ID. **Redis** is fast, has built-in expiry that suits abandoned carts, and keeps each cart as one simple key. Its downsides are an extra service to run, and carts can be lost or evicted unless persistence and memory policy are configured carefully. **Postgres** keeps carts durable and transactional, and you can query them for abandoned-cart emails or analytics. It costs a little more latency per read and needs a cleanup job for old carts. I recommend **Postgres** if you already run it, because carts are business data and durability and queryability matter more than the marginal speed gain. Redis makes more sense only if carts are truly disposable and you want the lowest latency.

input.title: Choose cart storage: Redis or Postgres
input.body:
Carts currently live in a 4 KB session cookie, so long carts get truncated. Moving carts server-side fixes this. The cookie would hold only a cart ID.

- **Postgres:** durable, transactional, queryable (abandoned-cart emails, analytics). Slightly higher read latency; needs a cleanup job for old carts.
- **Redis:** very fast, native TTL expiry. Needs an extra service, and carts can be lost or evicted unless persistence and memory policy are configured.

Recommendation: Postgres, assuming it is already in your stack.

content.text:
A1 [open] decision: Choose cart storage: Redis or Postgres
actions: a1 resolve "Postgres (Recommended)", a2 resolve "Redis"
